title: MTG Arena Limited for Beginners | How to Play, Sealed vs Draft, Building a 40-Card Deck

view.sub: How to play on MTG Arena, from scratch

scenes.say: New to Limited on MTG Arena? Let's go through how to play, from scratch.

view.sub: Play with only the cards you open

scenes.say: In Limited, you play with only the cards you open on the spot. You don't need a collection, so you can start right away.

view.name: MTG Arena
view.tag: The official digital version of Magic: The Gathering

scenes.say: MTG Arena is the official digital version of Magic. You can play on PC or on your phone, and it's free to play. The app handles the tricky rules for you, so you can learn as you play.
First, the basics. Games are one on one. You both start at 20 life, and you win by bringing your opponent to zero.
Each turn goes in this order: untap, draw, play, attack, and end.
Mana is the energy you use to cast spells, and it comes from lands. You can play only one land per turn, so the longer the game goes, the bigger the cards you can cast.

Cards come in five colours, and each colour is good at different things. White protects with lots of small creatures. Blue draws cards and counters spells. Black destroys creatures. Red deals damage. And green has big creatures.
In Limited, you usually build a two-colour deck.
Here's how to read a card. The name is at the top left, and the mana cost is at the top right. Serra Angel costs two white mana plus three mana of any colour, so five mana in total.
The four slash four at the bottom right is power and toughness. It deals four damage, and it dies when it takes four damage.

rows: Just an entry fee, same start for all

scenes.say: There are two main ways to play: Constructed and Limited. In Constructed, you build a 60-card deck from your collection. In Limited, you build a 40-card deck from only the packs you open. Everyone starts on equal terms, so your collection doesn't matter.
Limited has two formats: Sealed and Draft. In Sealed, you open six packs at once and build your deck from them. You can take your time on your own, so it's a good way to get used to deckbuilding.
In Draft, eight players each open a pack, take one card, and pass the rest along. Over three packs, you pick 42 cards.

rows: Right after a new set's release

scenes.say: On Arena, there are two kinds of Draft: Quick Draft and Premier Draft.
In Quick Draft, you draft with computer players. There's no pick timer, so you can go at your own pace. It costs about half as much as Premier Draft.
In Premier Draft, you sit at a table with seven other real players. Each pick has a timer, and the entry fee is higher, but so are the prizes.
Either way, your opponents in games are real players. If you're new to Draft, start with Quick Draft.

scenes.say: Limited on Arena isn't always the same set. Events follow the official event schedule. When a new set comes out, its Premier Draft and Sealed start first. Quick Draft rotates through sets by period, so older sets come around too, not just the newest one.
Your deck is 40 cards. If you're not sure, start with 17 lands, 17 creatures, and 6 other spells.
For the 23 non-land cards, lean towards cheap ones. Around six two-drops help you avoid hands where you can't do anything early.
Stick to two colours, and split your lands to match, like nine and eight.
Among your spells, removal comes first. Removal means cards that destroy your opponent's creatures, or stop them from attacking and blocking.

In Limited, your opponent will play big creatures and flyers too. One removal spell can stop them. And there are only a few removal spells in each pack, so in Draft, taking them early makes a difference.
Rarity and strength are different things. There are plenty of strong commons.

When in doubt, check the win rate when drawn. If a card is about three points above its set's average, it's a strong card. You can find the numbers for each set in this channel's format reviews and in the format reports on our site.

If you're nervous about jumping straight in, you can practise on our site. Sealed and Draft practice are free, as often as you like. You can open virtual packs and go all the way to building a deck. And when you play on Arena on PC, you can also use the Sealed and Draft assistants.
To sum up: in Limited, you build a 40-card deck from the packs you open. Aim for 17 lands, 17 creatures, and 6 spells, play two colours, and don't forget removal. For Draft, start with Quick Draft.
We also make a format review for every set, so please subscribe!
